questions.scenario: Your school is hosting a grand Diwali Mela. What is your role at your class stall?

options.text: Coming up with a completely unique game idea no one has seen before.
Standing in the front, shouting, and convincing crowds to play your game.
Testing the game to make sure it is actually fun and not too hard.
Managing the cash box, tokens, and making sure prizes don't run out.

questions.scenario: You want to earn some extra pocket money. What is your strategy?

options.text: Start a brand new service in school that no one else is doing.
Promote a friend's talent (like sketching) and take a 20% commission.
Listen to what students complain about the most and find a fix for it.
Buy popular pens/snacks in bulk for cheap and sell them for a small profit.

questions.scenario: When you watch a show like 'Shark Tank', what runs through your mind?

options.text: I imagine myself pitching my own crazy, billion-dollar idea.
I notice how confidently the person talks and sells their story.
I look at the product and think about how to improve its design.
I wonder how they manufacture, pack, and deliver 10,000 orders so fast.

questions.scenario: The school canteen always has a massive, crowded line. How do you solve this?

options.text: Propose opening a completely new, modern cafe on the other side of school.
Create attractive combo-meal posters so students buy food faster.
Change the menu to remove items that take too much time to cook.
Create a pre-booking token system so students just pick up and leave.

questions.scenario: If you had a 'Business Superpower', what would it be?

options.text: Fearlessness: I am never afraid to take massive risks.
Persuasion: I can talk anyone into believing my idea.
Mind-Reading: I know exactly what people need before they ask.
Speed: I can organize and deliver things faster than anyone else.

questions.scenario: Your group's master plan for a project completely fails at the last minute. What do you do?

options.text: Throw the old plan away and start a new, crazy idea from zero.
Smile confidently and convince the teacher that it wasn't a total failure.
Sit down, find the exact 'bug' that ruined the project, and fix it.
Quickly arrange for backup charts and materials from another class.

questions.scenario: How do you generally use social media (Instagram/YouTube)?

options.text: Watching videos of self-made billionaires and their life journeys.
Looking at viral trends and figuring out how to get maximum likes.
Watching gadget/movie reviews to see if they are worth buying.
Browsing shopping apps to find the best deals and fastest delivery.

questions.scenario: A company launches a new shoe, but people are not buying it. Why do you think it failed?

options.text: The idea wasn't bold or different enough. It was boring.
The advertisement was bad, and nobody knew about the shoe.
The shoe was uncomfortable or looked ugly when worn.
It was out of stock on Amazon or delivery took too many days.

questions.scenario: Every business has a 'boring/hard' part. Which one can you handle the best?

options.text: Getting rejected 50 times before one person finally says 'Yes'.
Smiling and talking nicely to a very rude and angry customer.
Listening to 100 complaints about your work and correcting them.
Doing the boring math of packing, shipping, and tracking items.

questions.scenario: What is the best compliment a friend could give you?

options.text: 'You always think so outside the box!'
'You can convince anybody to do anything!'
'You always know exactly how to fix my problems.'
'You are so organized, fast, and reliable.'
